previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of paraplegia, neurogenic bladder with chronic indwelling Foley catheter, type 2 diabetes, and foot ulcer s/p left TMA was admitted for diffuse abdominal pain and left flank pain. Evaluation revealed a complicated urinary tract infection due to E. coli and significant fecal loading causing constipation. She was treated with IV antibiotics initially, then transitioned to oral cefpodoxime for a 14-day course. Her abdominal pain improved after disimpaction and bowel regimen optimization. Due to persistently elevated blood glucose levels in the 200s–400s, her Lantus insulin was increased from 10 to 20 units at bedtime. The central line placed for IV access was removed prior to discharge. She was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to complete antibiotics, monitor blood sugar, and maintain bowel and wound care routines.

INDICATION:  Type 2 diabetes, neurogenic bladder with history of recurrent
UTIs, pyelonephritis and nephrolithiasis, now with left-sided flank pain,
likely pyelonephritis, please assess for abscess or obstruction.

COMPARISON:  CTU of ___.  Renal ultrasound of ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Renal ultrasound.

FINDINGS:

The right kidney measures 11.9 cm.  There is minimal pelvicaliectasis on the
right, which appears grossly unchanged from the CTU of ___, though
not seen on the ultrasound of ___.  No evidence of renal stones or
masses.  The left kidney measures 10.1 cm.  No stones, masses, or
hydronephrosis are identified on the left.  A cortical cleft or focus of
scarring is seen in the junction of the upper pole and interpolar region.  The
urinary bladder is collapsed about a Foley catheter.

IMPRESSION:

No evidence of renal stones, masses, or hydronephrosis.  Minimal
pelvicaliectasis of the right kidney was not seen on the ultrasound of ___,
but is probably unchanged in comparison with CT of ___.  No
left-sided hydronephrosis or evidence of abscess, as questioned.

SINGLE FRONTAL VIEW OF THE CHEST

REASON FOR EXAM:  Assess line.

The right subclavian vein catheter has two loops at the level of the right
subclavian vein, should be repositioned.  Cardiac size is normal.  The lungs
are clear.  There is no pneumothorax or pleural effusion.

Findings were discussed with IV nurse, ___, by phone on ___ at 10:31
a.m., one minute after discovery of the finding.

INDICATION:  Pyelonephritis, in need of intravenous antibiotics.  Recent
cathter placement could not be advanced beyond subclavian vein at bedside. 
Request for PICC placement.
 
OPERATORS: ___ NP  Dr. ___ (resident) and Dr. ___
___ (attending).

PROCEDURE AND FINDINGS:  The patient was brought to the angiographic suite and
laid supine on the fluoroscopic table.  The right arm with indwelling catheter
was prepped and draped in the usual sterile fashion.  A pre-procedure huddle
and timeout were performed per ___ protocol.
 
An initial scout demonstrated presence of the indwelling catheter with tip in
the proximal subclavian vein.  1% lidocaine was infiltrated into the
subcutaneous tissues adjacent to the catheter insertion site.  The catheter
was divided and a wire advanced to the IVC.  The catheter remnant was removed
and a peel away sheath placed.  Appropriate measurements were then made and
the wire was again advanced to the IVC.  The inner stiffener of the sheath was
removed and a dual-lumen 5 ___ PICC with internal length of 43 cm was
placed with tip in the distal SVC.  Final fluoroscopic image confirms
positioning in distal SVC/images saved.
 
The patient tolerated the procedure well and there were no immediate
post-procedure complications.
 
IMPRESSION:  Successful uncomplicated placement of right-sided 5 ___
dual-lumen PICC, measuring 43 cm internally with tip in the distal SVC.  The
line is ready to use.
